::: {.why}
The comparison you ran last night is the one that made practitioners abandon raw mean-variance, and running it yourself is more convincing than any paper on the subject.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the out-of-sample volatility and return of an optimised portfolio against equal weighting on your own data.
- State how many observations per asset you would need before the optimised solution reliably beats equal weighting.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Do the resampling experiment: draw 200 bootstrap samples of your return history, optimise on each, and plot all 200 frontiers on one axis. The width of that band, not the single line you drew on day 99, is the honest picture of what you know about the frontier.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Find the crossover empirically: run the split-sample comparison against equal weighting at estimation windows of 60, 120, 240 and 600 months, for 10 and 25 assets. Report a table of out-of-sample Sharpe for each cell, and read off where optimisation starts winning.
:::
:::
